stem: What is the usual long-term prognosis for most children with food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES)?

options.text: It is a lifelong condition requiring strict avoidance
It frequently progresses to IgE-mediated anaphylaxis
Most children outgrow the condition by 2 to 4 years of age
Resolution only occurs if the child also has severe eczema
It commonly causes permanent growth failure

explanation: Most children outgrow FPIES by 2 to 4 years of age, so the prognosis is generally favourable in early childhood.
rationale: FPIES is usually a transient non-IgE food allergy, and many children develop tolerance within the first few years of life.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because FPIES is usually not lifelong, and many children eventually tolerate the trigger food.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because FPIES is a non-IgE-mediated disorder and does not typically progress to IgE-mediated anaphylaxis.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because most children develop tolerance and outgrow FPIES by 2 to 4 years of age.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because FPIES resolution is not dependent on eczema or other atopic conditions.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because while feeding issues can occur, permanent growth failure is not the usual long-term outcome.

source.hint: Consider the typical age range for achieving tolerance to FPIES triggers.
